guide_q: how is a transaction measured against the size limit of a block?
note: guide_q / agent / root: the questions the page test asks the guide and one agent; chapter-specific, so the test can check that the guide hands over to the right agent. The Transaction agent has executed examples (transaction weight, identifiers, serialization), so a follow-up asking for an example can be answered, and it is not the largest agent (the Block agent is), which the test uses for its earlier questions. The three switches say what SEN0401 does not (yet) have, so the checks that need it are skipped and listed rather than failed: corpus_kinds = the kinds of passage the agents search (no textbook or course ontology); course_outcomes = a course ontology with LO-n outcomes; code_layers = concept examples that are Python programs (ontology graph syntax and behaviour layers). The question bank of chapter 3 is complete (an item for every concept), so bank_complete is not set to false. The corpus_kinds switch now lists book as well: the page embeds the ontology of its own chapter of Mastering Bitcoin, 3rd edition (mastering-bitcoin-3e, at a pinned commit), so the agents really do rank over book passages and the check that counts the kinds must expect one. course_outcomes stays false until SEN0401's own course-level ontologies exist; when they do, the corpus gains a course kind too and this switch is bumped again.
